source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Legal Aid Alberta
entries.description: Legal Aid Alberta provides lawyers and legal help to Albertans who meet its financial eligibility guidelines, in family, criminal, immigration and refugee, mental health and civil law matters. Its family law help covers parenting, guardianship, child support, divorce and child welfare matters, and its duty counsel lawyers assist people without a lawyer in courtrooms across Alberta.
entries.cost_note: Most services are not free: lawyers charge a reduced rate of $125.00 an hour plus fees, and clients repay Legal Aid Alberta through an interest-free repayment plan.
entries.evidence: We help with matters related to parenting, guardianship, child support, property actions, spousal support, and divorce.
entries.notes: Serves the whole province; people apply by phone (Monday to Friday, 8:15 a.m. to 4:15 p.m.), number from the Contact page; the mailing address is in Edmonton. The Help Centre answer says it helps citizens of all ages. Child counsel in high-conflict family cases is not free; parents pay for it.

entries.name: Persons with Developmental Disabilities (PDD)
entries.description: An Alberta government program that helps adults with a developmental disability plan, coordinate and access services so they can live as independently as they can in their community. Depending on each person's support plan, services can include home living supports, community access, employment supports, respite for family caregivers and specialized supports. People can apply from age 16, and services start at 18.
entries.cost_note: A government program; the pages do not mention fees. PDD does not provide income (that is AISH or ADAP).
entries.evidence: The Persons with Developmental Disabilities (PDD) program helps eligible adults plan, coordinate and access services to live as independently as they can in their community.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.pdd.org/; that no longer works (it is now a parked domain that redirects to a 'lander' page). The program's current page is on alberta.ca. Eligibility needs a developmental disability from before age 18, confirmed by a registered psychologist's assessment (IQ of 70 or lower). Phone is the Alberta Supports Contact Centre, from the How to apply page.

entries.name: Alberta Children's Hospital
entries.description: Alberta Health Services' children's hospital in Calgary, with a 24/7 emergency department and many clinics for children under 18. Its services include pediatric psychology, neuropsychology, speech-language pathology and occupational therapy, and a Neurodevelopmental Disorder Program that coordinates care for children with complex needs who are diagnosed with conditions such as autism or ADHD.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.address: 28 Oki Drive NW Calgary, Alberta, T3B 6A8
entries.evidence: This facility provides a range of healthcare services for children less than 18 years of age including a 24/7 emergency department.
entries.notes: CNAF gives an old address (1820 Richmond Road S.W.); the current address is from the AHS facility page, and the phone is the switchboard. CNAF says the hospital offers autism assessment by physician referral; the current pages list a Neurodevelopmental Disorder care coordination program (for children already diagnosed; 403-955-7281) but did not confirm an autism diagnostic clinic.

entries.name: Glenrose Rehabilitation Hospital
entries.description: An Alberta Health Services rehabilitation hospital in Edmonton for patients of all ages. For children with a question of autism it runs the Infant and Preschool Assessment & Outreach Service (6 months to kindergarten) and the School Age Neurodevelopmental Assessment & Outreach Clinic (ages 6 to 18), and it also has an Adult Autism Diagnostic Clinic. Health care providers make the referrals.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The School-Age Neurodevelopmental Clinic sees children when there is a question of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.albertahealthservices.ca/facilities/grh/; that no longer works ('Page Not Found'). The hospital's current AHS page is https://www.albertahealthservices.ca/grh/grh.aspx (reached from https://www.ahs.ca/grh). Clinic phones: preschool service 780-735-7998, school-age clinic central intake 780-735-6115. Both need earlier testing by an SLP, OT or psychologist that gives reasons for an autism assessment; some assessments can be virtual.

entries.name: Amundson Psychology & Consulting
entries.description: A Calgary psychology practice offering assessment and therapy for individuals, couples and families, including family and child therapy for children, teens and parents. Its team includes registered psychologist Zane Webber, who works with children, teens and their parents on family conflict, anxiety and anger. Appointments are in person or by telehealth.
entries.cost_note: The site does not list fees.
entries.address: Suite #2, 2005 37 Street SW, Calgary, Alberta T3E 3A5
entries.evidence: Support for children, teens, and parents to build resilience, address behavioural concerns, and foster family connection.
entries.notes: CNAF lists psychologist Zane C Webber at 'Amundson & Associates' (old address 1017 1 Ave NE). CNAF links to http://amundsonandassociates.com/, which now redirects to https://aapsych.ca/ (Amundson Psychology & Consulting, at a new address); Zane C. Webber is still on the team page. Address and phone from the home page; the email address is hidden behind a script.

entries.name: High Point Psychology
entries.description: A Calgary psychology practice that does psychological assessment and counselling for children, adolescents and adults. Its psychologists assess learning disorders, intellectual ability, autism, ADHD and other neurodevelopmental, mood and anxiety concerns, and offer therapy and support to children, youth and families.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the pages read; the site mentions billing and a Low Cost Counselling and Assessment Program with a practicum student. The clinical director offers free 15-minute phone consultations.
entries.address: #226 - 259 Midpark Way SE Calgary, AB T2X 1M2
entries.evidence: High Point Psychology is a Calgary-based psychology practice specializing in psychological assessment and counselling for children, adolescents, and adults.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (the About page) still works. Contact details from the Contact page. It also has a satellite office in Fort St. John, BC. The Services and Autism pages load by script and could not be read.

entries.name: Constellation Psychology
entries.description: A Calgary clinic of registered psychologists that does psychological and psychoeducational assessments for children, teens and adults, including autism, ADHD, learning disability, giftedness and intellectual disability assessments. It sees clients in person in Calgary and offers virtual assessments in several provinces and the NWT.
entries.cost_note: $235.00 an hour (Psychologists' Association of Alberta fee schedule) with flat-rate assessments; direct billing to most major insurers; a free 15-minute consultation.
entries.address: 1925 18 Ave NE, Suite #115 (Smart Executive Centre) Calgary, AB T2E 7T8
entries.evidence: We work with children, teens, and adults across the lifespan from families seeking answers about a child’s learning or development, to adults exploring a possible ADHD or autism profile for the first time.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Sharon Blott Psychological Services; http://sharonblott.com/ now redirects to https://constellationpsychology.ca/. The About page says the clinic was rebranded as Constellation Psychology in March 2024 and Sharon Blott is still one of its psychologists; the phone is the one CNAF lists. Fees from the Fees page (it lists an autism assessment for children and teens).

entries.name: Insight Solutions Psychology Inc.
entries.description: A Calgary psychology practice run by registered psychologist Paloma Scott, offering online and in-person counselling for children, teens, adults, couples and families. For children it uses play-based therapy, starting with an appointment for parents only, and it works with children who have ADHD, autism (ASD) or anxiety.
entries.cost_note: $300 an hour; direct billing to insurance where available; no free consultations.
entries.evidence: I specialize in working with children experiencing ADHD, ASD, and anxiety.
entries.notes: CNAF lists psychologist Paloma Scott with a link to her Jane booking page, which still works and names her practice, Insight Solutions Psychology Inc. (the booking page has moved from the Midnapore location to the Heritage Professional Building). The booking page says she is a registered FSCD provider; email from that page.

entries.name: Behaviour Therapy and Learning Centre (BTLC)
entries.description: A Calgary charity that runs Program Unit Funded (PUF) preschool and kindergarten programs for children aged 2½ to 6 with autism or other developmental delays, using Applied Behaviour Analysis. Children learn in a small onsite specialized classroom or with a trained aide in a community preschool or kindergarten, each with an Individualized Program Plan.
entries.cost_note: Programs are Program Unit Funded (PUF); the site does not mention fees for families.
entries.address: Suite 100, 5970 Centre Street SE Calgary, AB T2H 0C1
entries.evidence: Programs and services are provided to children between the ages of 2 ½ to 6, living in Calgary and surrounding communities (e.g. Airdrie).
entries.notes: CNAF lists BTLC twice (under Pre School Education Program and, as 'Big Things Can Happen', under Therapies); http://www.btlc.ca/ now redirects to https://btlc.ca/. Contact details from the Contact page. The site carries no dates and looks little updated; its Events page has nothing scheduled.

entries.name: Cause & Effect Foundation
entries.description: A Calgary charity running an early intervention program that provides speech and language services, mostly in daycare settings in Calgary and nearby communities, to children with special needs aged 3 years 8 months to 6 years. Its programs are funded by Alberta Education grants.
entries.cost_note: The site says there is no cost to parents; funding comes from Alberta Education's Mild/Moderate (MM) and Moderate Language Delay (PUF-MLD) grants.
entries.evidence: We provide speech and language services, primarily in daycare settings within Calgary and surrounding communities, to children aged 3 years 8 months to 6 years.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://causeandeffectfoundation.com/; that no longer works (it redirects to https without www and returns Cloudflare error 526, invalid SSL certificate). The organisation's site works at https://www.causeandeffectfoundation.com/. CNAF's description (ages 6 months to 6, in-home settings) is older than the site's. Contact details from the home page.

entries.name: New Heights School & Learning Services
entries.description: A Calgary charity and Designated Special Education Private School for students on the autism spectrum, with a kindergarten and Grades 1-12 program, a transition-to-adulthood network for graduates up to age 25, and an FSCD-funded Home & Community Support Program. Classes are small, with teachers, psychologists, occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists and educational assistants.
entries.cost_note: Grade K-12 tuition is $14,000 per school year plus a $100 application fee; the Home & Community Support Program is funded through FSCD. The site has a Financial Assistance page.
entries.address: 85 Normandy Drive SW Calgary, AB T3E 7J9
entries.evidence: New Heights School & Learning Services is a registered charitable organization and a Designated Special Education Private School.
entries.notes: CNAF's link http://www.newheightscalgary.com/aboutus now redirects to https://www.newheightscalgary.com/about/. Phone and address from the About and Contact pages (Home and Community Support: 403.250.1317). News posts are dated October 2026.

entries.name: Pacekids
entries.description: A Calgary charity for children with diverse needs such as speech and language delay, cerebral palsy and developmental delays. It runs therapy-integrated preschool and kindergarten (Early Childhood Services) for ages 2.8 to 6 through Program Unit Funding, and FSCD-funded community and in-home support, including Triple P parenting, for children aged 2 to 10.
entries.cost_note: ECS programs are funded through Program Unit Funding (PUF) and in-home services through FSCD; the site does not mention fees.
entries.address: #130 2850 Sunridge Blvd NE, Calgary, AB T1Y 6G2
entries.evidence: Pacekids supports children with diverse needs, including speech and language delay, cerebral palsy, global developmental delay, brain injury, and other developmental delays and disabilities.
entries.notes: http://www.pacekids.ca/ now redirects to https://pacekids.ca/. Second location: #130 23 Sunpark Drive SE, Calgary. It also runs a pilot Triple P program for families of teens aged 13 to 16 with disabilities. The email address is hidden behind a script.

entries.name: Diverse Learning Needs (Calgary Board of Education)
entries.description: The Calgary Board of Education's supports for students with diverse learning needs, from help in the community school with an Individualized Program Plan to referral for specialized classes or unique settings. It covers students who are blind or deaf, gifted, or have complex learning and medical needs, learning disabilities, or behaviour and mental health needs.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The CBE provides a continuum of supports and services for students with diverse learning needs.
entries.notes: CNAF lists this as 'Guide to Education for Students with Special Needs'; https://cbe.ab.ca/diverse-learning-needs redirects to the www page (last modified August 2026). Phone and email are the CBE Inclusive Education team's; the address is the CBE main office (Education Centre).

entries.name: Grants for Students with Disabilities (Alberta Student Aid)
entries.description: Alberta Student Aid's funding for post-secondary students with a permanent, or persistent or prolonged, disability. Approved students can get the Canada Student Grant for Students with Disabilities, up to $20,000 a year for assistive services and equipment (or the Alberta Grant for Students with Disabilities, up to $3,000), can study at a reduced course load while keeping full-time aid, and can be reimbursed for disability assessment costs.
entries.cost_note: A government student aid program (loans and grants); the page does not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: If you are approved as a student with a disability (either a PD or a PPD), you may be eligible to receive up to $20,000 per loan year to help you with exceptional education-related costs such as assistive services or equipment.
entries.notes: CNAF links to studentaid.alberta.ca (still current), its Applications and Forms page, an old Schedule 4 PDF (now 404) and an old 'students with permanent disabilities' page (now 404); this entry covers all four. The current details are in Chapter 5 of the Loans and Grants Funding Guide: students apply for student aid, then send a Schedule 4 with disability documentation, part of it completed by the school's accessibility advisor. Phone is the Alberta Student Aid Service Centre.

entries.name: Disability Related Employment Supports (DRES)
entries.description: Alberta government funding for supports that help people with disabilities with job search, work, or education and training toward a job, such as assistive devices and technology, ASL interpreting and captioning, academic aides or note takers, and workplace or vehicle modifications. It is for Albertans aged 16 or older with a documented, permanent or long-term disability who are working or heading to work, but not for students in Alberta K-12 or publicly funded post-secondary programs.
entries.cost_note: A government funding program; the page does not mention any fee.
entries.evidence: DRES provides funding for supports and services that help Albertans overcome disability related barriers to employment or education.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old humanservices.alberta.ca page (now 'Page not found'); the program's current page is on alberta.ca. People apply through an Alberta Supports Centre; the phone is the Alberta Supports Contact Centre.

entries.name: Family Support for Children with Disabilities (FSCD)
entries.description: An Alberta government program that works with families of children with disabilities under 18 to plan, coordinate and get supports and services. Depending on assessed needs this can include information and referral, respite, counselling, aides for personal care or behavioural and developmental support, help with some disability-related costs, and specialized services for children with severe disabilities. A child who is still waiting for a diagnosis can be eligible.
entries.cost_note: A government program; the pages do not mention fees for its services. Families pay any fee a health professional charges to write the medical letter needed to apply.
entries.evidence: The FSCD program works with eligible families to provide support and services based on each child and family’s needs.
entries.notes: CNAF links to several old FSCD pages on humanservices.alberta.ca and child.alberta.ca ('Support for Children with Disabilities', 'FSCD Eligibility and Application Process', 'FSCD Services', and FSCD again under Services/Service Providers); they now give 'Page not found' or the general Children and Family Services page. This entry covers all of them. Families apply online; phone is the Alberta Supports Contact Centre (How to apply page). FSCD does not provide financial benefits or individual therapy.

entries.name: Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH)
entries.description: An Alberta government program that pays a monthly living allowance and health benefits to adults with a severe, permanent disability that prevents them from working, with possible child and personal benefits. Applicants must be 18 or older, not yet eligible for Old Age Security, live in Alberta and meet financial criteria. One combined Disability Income Assistance application covers both AISH and the Alberta Disability Assistance Program (ADAP).
entries.cost_note: A government income and health benefit; the pages do not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: Provides financial and health benefits for eligible Albertans with a severe disability that is permanent and prevents employment.
entries.notes: CNAF links to old humanservices.alberta.ca AISH pages and an AISH tip sheet (all 'Page not found'); the program's current page is on alberta.ca. Applications go through the single Disability Income Assistance application and are reviewed in the order received. Phone is the Alberta Supports Contact Centre, from the Disability Income Assistance page.

entries.name: Early Childhood Services (ECS) Pre-Kindergarten
entries.description: Alberta-funded Pre-Kindergarten programming for children who need extra support before Kindergarten, including children diagnosed with a mild, moderate or severe disability or a moderate or severe language delay. Children with a severe disability or a moderate or severe language delay can start at 2 years 8 months; families register through their local school board or an independent ECS operator.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention fees; programs are run by school boards and independent ECS operators.
entries.evidence: Pre-Kindergarten is for children who require additional supports to prepare them for Kindergarten and Grade 1.
entries.notes: CNAF describes Program Unit Funding (PUF), Alberta Education funding to approved ECS operators for young children with a severe disability or delay, and links to an education.alberta.ca ECS page that now says it has moved to alberta.ca/early-childhood-education. That page describes the Pre-Kindergarten programming PUF pays for but does not name PUF; no current PUF page was found (alberta.ca/program-unit-funding returns 404). BTLC, Pacekids, Providence and Cause & Effect Foundation in this file say they are PUF-funded.

entries.name: Special Needs Assistance for Seniors
entries.description: An Alberta government benefit that helps low-income seniors aged 65 and older pay for specific health supports, personal supports, and appliances or furniture, up to a yearly maximum. Eligibility depends on income, marital status and accommodation, and seniors must have applied for Seniors Financial Assistance.
entries.cost_note: A benefit of up to $5,872 per benefit year (July 1 to June 30); the page does not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: Seniors with low-income can get financial assistance to help afford the cost of appliances and specific health and personal supports.
entries.notes: CNAF's old seniors.alberta.ca link now redirects to this alberta.ca page. The information booklet PDF CNAF also links returns 404; the page links a current information sheet instead. Phone is the Alberta Supports Contact Centre.

entries.name: Alberta Human Rights Commission
entries.description: An independent commission of the Government of Alberta that works under the Alberta Human Rights Act to reduce discrimination, including at work, in housing and in services. People who believe they were discriminated against in Alberta can get information from its Confidential Inquiry Line and make a complaint within one year of what happened.
entries.cost_note: The Commission does not charge any fees to take part in the complaint process.
entries.evidence: Our mandate is to foster equality and reduce discrimination. We do so by providing public information and education programs, and by helping people resolve human rights complaints.
entries.notes: CNAF lists the 'Alberta Human Rights and Citizenship Commission' with a link to an old mandate page (http://www.albertahumanrights.ab.ca/ahrcc/Mandate_Function_of_Comm.asp, now 404); the Commission's current site is https://albertahumanrights.ab.ca/. Phone is the Confidential Inquiry Line (toll-free by dialling 310-0000 first); offices in Edmonton and Calgary.

entries.name: Special Olympics Alberta
entries.description: A charity that runs year-round sports training and competition for children and adults with intellectual disabilities in communities across Alberta. Athletes register online and train weekly in sports such as swimming, softball, floor curling, pickleball and fitness programs.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Special Olympics Alberta provides year-round sports programs for individuals with intellectual disabilities, fostering inclusion, empowerment, and community engagement through sports.
entries.notes: http://www.specialolympics.ab.ca/ now redirects to https://www.specialolympics.ab.ca/. Phone and email are the provincial office's (Jerry Forbes Centre, Edmonton); the Contact page also lists Calgary and Edmonton offices. Charitable number 11878 1145 RR0001.

entries.name: Providence Child Development Society
entries.description: A Calgary charity that runs specialized preschool and kindergarten programs, with therapy built in, for children with a delay or disability such as autism, Down syndrome or speech and language delays. It has seven school locations, early intervention from 19 months, and programs for children aged 2.8 to six funded through Alberta Education's Program Unit Funding (PUF).
entries.cost_note: Programs are funded by Alberta Education; the only fee is a non-refundable annual registration fee of $50. Busing within Calgary may be free for eligible children.
entries.evidence: Our school program operates at seven locations across Calgary with programs for children ages 2.8 to six years old, and early intervention beginning at 19 months.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://providencechildren.com/programs/school-program-details/; that no longer works ('Page not found'). The same organisation's current program page is https://www.providencechildren.com/our-schools/. A child must qualify for PUF (a diagnosed developmental delay, disability or medical condition) and Providence applies for it. Address is the head office (Windsor Park School).

entries.name: Khan Communication Services Inc.
entries.description: An Edmonton clinic of speech-language pathologists, occupational and physical therapists, psychologists and behaviour consultants serving children, teens and young adults, families and schools, online and in person. It does interdisciplinary autism assessments and runs the CHATTER social skills groups for children and teens.
entries.cost_note: A fee structure is discussed at the first consult; it accepts families with FSCD funding but is no longer taking FSCD-funded families for individual treatment.
entries.address: 5328 Admiral Girouard Street, Suite 201 Edmonton, Alberta T5E 6Z7
entries.evidence: Highly experienced and caring Psychologists, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Occupational Therapists work together to provide an interdisciplinary assessment for children, adolescents, and young adults.
entries.notes: http://www.khancommunicationservices.com/ now redirects to https://www.khancommunicationservices.com/. The home page says it is no longer accepting FSCD-funded families for individual treatment, though they can apply for the Chatter group program. Address from the Contact page.

entries.name: JB Music Therapy
entries.description: A Calgary team of certified music therapists working in schools, hospitals, disability programs, continuing care and mental health settings, with online music therapy for people elsewhere. In schools they support children and students with autism, ADHD and developmental disabilities.
entries.cost_note: The site does not list fees.
entries.evidence: In school settings, our music therapists collaborate with educators, support staff, and other specialists to support children and students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), and developmental disabilities.
entries.notes: http://jbmusictherapy.com/ now redirects to https://jbmusictherapy.com/. Much of its work is through partner organisations (schools, hospitals, care homes); no street address is given.

entries.name: Music Therapy Association for Alberta (MTAA)
entries.description: The provincial association for Certified Music Therapists (MTA) in Alberta. It promotes music therapy and public awareness of it in Alberta, and its website has a Find a Music Therapist directory.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The MTAA represents Certified Music Therapists (MTA) at the provincial level.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (http://www.mtaa.ca/?page_id=26) now loads the association's home page on https. The Find a Music Therapist page loads by script and its listings could not be read. Email from the Contact page.

entries.name: Autism Partnership
entries.description: The Calgary office of Autism Partnership, which provides individualized behavioural intervention programs based on Applied Behaviour Analysis for autistic children and their families. It runs an early intervention program for ages 18 months to 6 years and a program for school-aged children 7 to 12, delivered at home, in the community and at its clinic, plus group programs and parent workshops.
entries.cost_note: A private agency: programs can be funded largely through FSCD, by insurance or by private payment.
entries.evidence: A comprehensive and highly individualized program for children with autism aged 18 months to 6 years, designed to help them develop skills to thrive and be lifelong learners, ready for school and beyond.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.autismpartnership.com/ (the head office in California); its Canadian office, https://www.autismpartnership.ca/, is in Calgary, so it is listed here. BTLC's site also recommends Autism Partnership for FSCD home services. Assessment information is marked 'coming soon'.

entries.name: Children's Autism Services of Edmonton
entries.description: An Edmonton organisation founded in 2004 that offers family-centred autism services based on the SCERTS model. Families with an FSCD contract can get specialized and developmental support services at home from speech-language pathologists, occupational therapists, behaviour consultants and psychologists; it also runs an Early Education Program (ages 2.8 to 6), a school program, respite and community aide services, and free screenings for children aged 2 to 3.
entries.cost_note: Specialized and developmental services are accessed through an FSCD funding contract; screenings for children aged 2 to 3 are free; the site does not list other fees.
entries.evidence: Early Education programming is provided to children between 2.8 and 6 years of age, who have been diagnosed with a severe disability (including severe communication delays or behavioural challenges).
entries.notes: CNAF lists it twice: as Children's Autism Services of Edmonton (http://www.childrensautism.ca/net/) and as 'Stepping Stones Autism Institute (Children's Autism Services of Edmonton)' (http://www.childrensautism.ca/web/). Both links now give 'Page not found' on https://childrensautism.ca/, and the Stepping Stones name no longer appears on the site. Address is Maier Centre West; other sites are Maier Centre South and the Jim Jiwani Autism Academy.

entries.name: Renfrew Educational Services
entries.description: A Calgary charity and designated special education school for children with significant disabilities, such as autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy and global developmental delay. It runs Early Childhood Services and an elementary program (preschool to Grade 6) at four Calgary centres, plus community services such as private assessment and therapy and the Stepping Out on Saturdays respite program.
entries.cost_note: A resource fee of $100 a month for Early Childhood Services and a student fee of $450 a month for the full-day Elementary Education Program.
entries.evidence: Renfrew Educational Services is a registered Canadian charity and designated Special Education School in the province of Alberta.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (http://www.renfreweducation.org/Services-and-Programs/Programs.aspx) now gives 'Page not found' on https://renfreweducation.org/, the organisation's current site. A child needs a diagnosis or delay identified by a doctor or therapist and must meet Alberta Education funding criteria. Contact details are the main office (Janice McTighe Centre).

entries.name: Janus Academy
entries.description: A Calgary charity that runs a school for students diagnosed with autism aged 6 to 18, with individualized teaching based on Applied Behaviour Analysis and a modified Alberta Program of Studies. It also offers summer camps and community workshops.
entries.cost_note: Tuition for 2026-2027 is $17,140.00, plus a $200 non-refundable application fee; families commit to fundraising, and bursaries may cover part of tuition.
entries.evidence: Janus Academy operates a school for students diagnosed with ASD aged 6 to 18 years of age.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.janusacademy.com/; that no longer works (the domain is for sale on HugeDomains). The organisation now uses https://janusacademy.org/. Applications for 2027-2028 open October 1, 2026.

entries.name: Specialized Programming (Edmonton Public Schools)
entries.description: Edmonton Public Schools' specialized programs at select schools for students who need specialized learning supports, including students with moderate or severe autism and those with learning, cognitive, behavioural, communication, physical or medical needs. Families start with the principal of their designated school, and a Specialized Learning Supports team works with schools and families from Kindergarten to Grade 12.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Students enrolled in a specialized learning program will receive instruction determined by Alberta Education and Childcare, as well as specialized supports designed for their individual needs and abilities.
entries.notes: CNAF lists 'Edmonton Public School Board: Specialized Therapy Educational Play Program (STEPP) Waverly Elementary School' twice, linking to an Autism Society Canada directory page whose domain no longer resolves; STEPP is not named on epsb.ca now. This entry is the school division's current specialized programming page (students must meet eligibility and be referred by their principal); a reviewer may prefer to drop it. Phone and address are the Centre for Education.

entries.name: Entrepreneurs with Disabilities Program (EDP) in Alberta (PrairiesCan)
entries.description: A federal PrairiesCan program that gives entrepreneurs with disabilities business information, training, mentoring and one-on-one counselling, and in some locations business loans when they cannot get financing elsewhere. In Alberta it is delivered by Prospect Human Services in Edmonton, Momentum in Calgary and Community Futures offices in rural areas.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention fees; business loans are offered in some locations.
entries.evidence: Western Canadians with disabilities can access a network of business professionals and other resources through Prairies Economic Development Canada (PrairiesCan)’s Entrepreneurs with Disabilities Program (EDP).
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old servicecanada.gc.ca page (now landing on the general Service Canada page); its old target, Western Economic Diversification Canada's EDP page, is archived. The current PrairiesCan page (dated 2026-04-09) covers Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba; this entry is the Alberta part (Edmonton 780-705-9677, Calgary 403-272-9323, rural Alberta 1-877-482-3672). Eligibility includes being unable to get business funding from other sources and having a possible business plan.

entries.name: Creative Supports (Excel Society)
entries.description: Excel Society's home support and respite program for people with disabilities, mainly in Edmonton and Calgary. Excel Society also runs residential and day programs in Alberta for people with developmental disabilities and complex needs.
entries.cost_note: The page says it serves clients funded through PDD, NWT, Nunavut and Children’s Services; no fees are listed.
entries.evidence: Our Creative Supports Program offers exceptional home support and respite services for individuals with disabilities, primarily in Edmonton and Calgary, with expansion to surrounding areas.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Excel Society's 'Community Support Services Division I' on its Nunavut page because it serves people funded by Nunavut, the NWT and Alberta; the link (excelsociety.org/division1.html) returns 404, and the same service now appears as Creative Supports on the Community Living page. Services are in Alberta; head offices in Edmonton and Calgary ((403) 730-2117); intake inquiries go to intake@excelsociety.org.

entries.name: Neurodevelopmental and Autism Consultation Service (NDACS), Alberta Health Services
entries.description: An Alberta Health Services clinic at the Glenrose Rehabilitation Hospital in Edmonton for children and teens up to 17 with autism and/or other neurodevelopmental disorders who have complex medical, learning, emotional or behavioural needs. Families can consult developmental pediatricians, pediatric psychiatrists, nurses and social workers, with referral to other specialized services when needed. Referrals come from healthcare providers through the Alberta Referral Directory.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention fees for the service (only pay parking).
entries.evidence: NDACS provides specialized care to children and teens up to 17 years of age with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and / or other neurodevelopmental disorders (conditions that affect the development of the nervous system) with complex needs.
entries.notes: Listed by CNAF on its Saskatchewan page as 'Alberta Health Services ~ Autism Clinic'. CNAF's old services.asp link now errors, but the same service ID (1007810) on AHS's Find Healthcare site is this service, which lists 'Autism Clinic, Autism Follow-up Clinic, Autism Spectrum Disorder Follow-up Clinic' as previous names. Address, phone and hours (Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:15 pm) from the Glenrose location page; eligibility needs a confirmed diagnosis.
